verdicts.quote: In a class with a waiting member eligible for a spot, the member receives a confirmed booking without submitting another request.
If two otherwise eligible members join one after the other for the same class and only one spot opens, the earlier entrant receives it.
verdicts.missing: How simultaneous joins (ties) resolve, and whether any membership tier or staff override can jump the queue.

verdicts.quote: Cancelling a confirmed booking obtained from the waitlist has the same applicable credit return, refund or penalty as cancelling a comparable direct booking.
verdicts.missing: Whether a no-show on an automatically promoted booking (possibly promoted late) counts against the existing no-show policy.

verdicts.quote: When a spot opens during the booking window and at least one waiting member qualifies, an eligible waiting member receives the spot.
verdicts.missing: That allocation runs as background work and how promptly it must happen after the triggering cancellation or capacity change.

verdicts.quote: If an ordinary confirmed booking for this member and class gives a receipt or confirmation through the app's existing channels, a confirmed booking from the waitlist does too.
verdicts.missing: What the notification says (that it came from the waitlist), and what happens when sending fails or no existing channel exists.

verdicts.quote: Competing joins, allocations and direct booking requests cannot cause a new booking to take confirmed attendance beyond the configured capacity, including when requests arrive together.
If a waiting member acquires a confirmed booking for the same class through an existing booking path, the waitlist does not allocate another spot to that member.
For the same member, class and time of confirmation, any price charged follows the rules for an ordinary booking.
verdicts.missing: What happens when the charge for a promoted booking fails: whether the spot passes to the next member and whether the entry ends.

verdicts.quote: An otherwise valid join is not refused solely because of the number of members already waiting.
A spot that becomes available at or after the point when the class stops accepting ordinary bookings does not produce a waitlist booking.
raising capacity enough to add a bookable spot while waitlist allocation is open allows that spot to be filled from the waitlist.
Once the operator cancels or removes a class using a supported action, its entries cease to be active.
If the same entries remain active after a restart, their priority relative to each other remains the same.
verdicts.missing: The entry record's fields (join time, state) and whether position is stored or derived from join order.

verdicts.quote: A member who was waiting when the waitlist closed can no longer see an active waiting entry for the class.
verdicts.missing: What happens to entry records after the class has run and how long they are retained.

verdicts.quote: A caller who cannot see another member's booking status cannot obtain their individual waitlist status through the waitlist feature.
verdicts.missing: Whether a member sees their own queue position, or only that they are waiting.

verdicts.quote: an operator can accept waitlist joins for eligible full classes without setting additional options.
verdicts.missing: Whether the operator can turn the waitlist off globally or per class or class type.

verdicts.quote: An eligible member viewing an available class can still use the existing booking flow.
Members keep their existing bookings and can join the waitlist of an already-full class.
